test_cases.brief_summary: Digital-first local news outlet, 8 editorial staff (6 reporters, 1 EIC, 1 copy editor), 5 beats, daily M-F, introducing AI tools for first time, no existing policies — existing example, full 5-step pipeline
test_cases.editorial_naturalness_note: One structural tell: the five beat guides follow an identical template structure (Scope → Source Development → Recurring Story Types → AI Usage → Competitive Landscape) with competitive landscape sections that repeat the same advice pattern ('Your advantage is depth/consistency/follow-up'). The AI policy and ethics template are strong — 'If it did not happen, we do not publish it' is genuine editorial voice.

test_cases.brief_summary: 25-person newsroom, weekly print magazine plus daily digital, 8 beats, existing AI tools (ChatGPT, Otter), union constraints on AI usage — simulated deliverable, full pipeline, content-arc-planner included
test_cases.editorial_naturalness_note: Structural repetition across 8 beat guides becomes more pronounced at scale — the competitive landscape sections for beats like 'environment' and 'health' would lean toward the same generic differentiation advice. The AI policy for a unionized newsroom would need more specific language the agent may default to boilerplate for.

test_cases.brief_summary: 3-person digital investigative nonprofit, single beat (government accountability), monthly long-form plus breaking investigations, no AI tools, focused on establishing ethics and editorial protocols — simulated deliverable, content-arc included
test_cases.editorial_naturalness_note: Single-beat simplicity helps avoid the structural repetition problem. However, the agent's operations-package framing ('newsroom infrastructure') is slightly over-engineered for a 3-person team — a working investigative editor would produce a leaner document. The ethics template section is the strongest, naturally suited to the accountability focus.
